result.title: From Opinions to Commitments: Unstable Assignments and Silent Choices in AI-Mediated Proposals
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being used to turn citizens' opinions into collective proposals. These proposals can make assignments: who should act, what must be done, how much one should spend and by when. However, if the assignments change when the same opinions are processed again, publishing a single proposal can hide alternatives that participants never get to see. We examined this issue in four LLM mediators (three open-weight and one commercial) using opinions from DeliberationBank and Polis. For each task, a mediator drafted a proposal from thirty opinions five times, varying either the random seed or the order of the opinions. In 17% of five-run sets from the open-weight mediators and 20% from the commercial one, some runs contained assignments while others did not. Reordering the opinions changed the assignments almost as often as replacing them with opinions from different citizens. Three human annotators confirmed that the detected differences between runs were real, although the LLM judge overstated how often they occurred. Substantial variation remained under four safeguards: temperature zero, a commercial mediator, draft selection, and draft merging. The mediator's objective also shaped representation: prompts seeking agreement covered minority positions much less often than prompts asking to describe differences. A single proposal can therefore obscure choices in both the assignments it proposes and the views it excludes. We propose audits that make alternative assignments visible and disclose the objective behind each proposal.

AI.brief_summary: 该文考察四个 LLM 中介在把公民意见转化为集体提案时，重复运行或打乱意见顺序是否改变其中的任务分配，并评估温度、草案筛选与合并等防护措施及人类标注一致性，进而提出审计方案。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究的是文本审议提案的输出稳定性与少数意见代表性，不涉及视觉/多模态推理、latent 状态的生成与使用或证据获取与停止决策，缺少可供核查的具体借鉴线索。
